_metadata.description: Agent lookup index — subset of connector-registry.json. Contains fields needed by Scout/Analyst for system inference, gotcha detection, and stub creation. For Maven coordinates, configTemplate, propertiesRequired, and URLs, use connector-registry.json.

salesforce.notes: Supports SOAP API, REST API, Bulk API v1/v2, Streaming API, Platform Events, Change Data Capture. Use OAuth JWT bearer flow with dedicated integration user — never username/password in production.

salesforce-data-cloud.notes: Salesforce Data Cloud (formerly Salesforce CDP). Supports data ingestion, Data Lake queries, customer profile lookups, calculated insights. Closely integrated with Agentforce for AI-powered customer 360. NOTE: The older mule-salesforce-data-cloud-connector artifact is deprecated — use mule4-sdc-connector.

salesforce-marketing-cloud.notes: Uses Salesforce Marketing Cloud SOAP API and REST API.

salesforce-commerce-cloud-shop.notes: Salesforce Commerce Cloud B2C storefront APIs.

agentforce.notes: Connects Mule flows to Salesforce Agentforce AI agents. NAMESPACE PREFIX IS ms-agentforce (not agentforce). No invoke-agent operation — session lifecycle is explicit: start-agent-conversation → send-message-sync → end-agent-conversation. continue-agent-conversation is DEPRECATED in v1.3. Agent ID attribute is named 'agent' (not agentId). Error types use MS-AGENTFORCE: prefix. Always end session in try error-handler to prevent resource leaks. Use with mule-mcp-connector (MCP server/client) and mule4-a2a-connector (agent-to-agent) for full agentic architectures. Data Cloud connector (mule4-sdc-connector) provides the knowledge base layer. VERIFY-A: send-message-sync variable passing syntax. VERIFY-B: send-message-sync response field path.

einstein-ai.notes: Provides access to Salesforce Einstein prediction and language APIs.

salesforce-composite.notes: Batches multiple Salesforce REST API calls into a single HTTP request using the Composite API. Reduces API call count for bulk operations.

salesforce-einstein-analytics.notes: Connects to Salesforce Einstein Analytics (now Tableau CRM) for dataset upload and query operations.

salesforce-marketing-cloud-rest.notes: REST-based Marketing Cloud connector (complements the SOAP-based sfdc-marketing-cloud connector). Preferred for newer Marketing Cloud API calls.

salesforce-pubsub.notes: Connects to Salesforce Pub/Sub API (gRPC-based). Use for high-throughput Platform Events and Change Data Capture. Replaces the older Streaming API.

salesforce-b2c-commerce-data.notes: Salesforce B2C Commerce Cloud Data API for admin/management operations. Different from the Shop API connector which is for storefront.

netsuite.notes: Uses SuiteTalk SOAP API. NetSuite Connector 11.0+ does NOT support REST-based operations — that requires the separate NetSuite Restlet Connector or HTTP connector with OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials + PS256 JWT (which requires Java helper JAR using Nimbus JOSE library since native MuleSoft JWT module does not support PS256).

netsuite-restlet.notes: Connects to custom NetSuite RESTlets. Use when SOAP is insufficient or for custom script calls.

sap.notes: REQUIRES SEPARATE MULESOFT LICENSE — contact MuleSoft sales before including in project scope. Also requires SAP JCo libraries (sapjco3.jar). Supports RFC, IDoc, BAPI. CloudHub 2.0 supported with Certificate connection type.

sap-s4hana-cloud.notes: Connects to SAP S/4HANA Cloud REST APIs (OData services). Different from SAP JCo connector — no SAP license required for this one.

sap-concur.notes: Expense and travel management. Supports both SOAP and REST calls to Concur APIs.

workday.notes: Covers HR, Finance, Payroll, Recruiting modules via Workday Web Services SOAP API.

oracle-ebs-121.notes: Oracle EBS 12.1. For 12.2 use the oracle-ebs-122 connector.

oracle-ebs-122.notes: Oracle EBS 12.2 with REST-based interface support.

oracle-peoplesoft.notes: Uses PeopleSoft Component Interface and Integration Broker.

oracle-siebel.notes: Connects to Oracle Siebel CRM using Siebel Java Data Bean or EAI HTTP Transport.

microsoft-dynamics-365-finance-ops.notes: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations (D365FO) OData services. Enterprise ERP — different from D365 CRM.

quickbooks-online.notes: Intuit QuickBooks Online REST API v3.

quickbooks-enterprise.notes: stub — QuickBooks Desktop/Enterprise has NO REST API. Uses QBXML via Windows Web Connector. NO native MuleSoft connector. Integration options: CData JDBC Driver, Conductor REST wrapper, or direct QBXML/SOAP. Must confirm whether client can upgrade to QB Online. See FK-020 and standards/playbooks/quickbooks-enterprise/quickbooks-enterprise_playbook.json.

paylocity.notes: stub — No dedicated MuleSoft connector on Exchange. Use HTTP connector with OAuth2 Client Credentials. API access requires formal Web Services Access Request Form — multi-week approval. See FK-021 and standards/playbooks/paylocity/paylocity_playbook.json.

sap-successfactors.notes: SAP SuccessFactors HCM Suite OData APIs. Covers Employee Central, Recruiting, Onboarding, Learning modules.

sap-s4hana-soap.notes: SAP S/4HANA SOAP-based web services (WSDL). Use this for SOAP interfaces; use sap-s4hana-cloud for OData/REST.

oracle-erp-cloud.notes: Oracle Fusion ERP Cloud REST APIs. Covers Financials, Procurement, Project Management modules.

oracle-hcm-cloud.notes: Oracle Fusion HCM Cloud REST APIs. Covers HR, Payroll, Talent Management.

netsuite-openair.notes: NetSuite OpenAir PSA (Professional Services Automation) platform. Separate from the core NetSuite ERP connector.

zuora.notes: Zuora subscription billing and monetization platform REST API.

zuora-aqua.notes: Zuora AQuA API for bulk data export using ZOQL queries. Use for reporting and data warehouse loads.

xero.notes: Xero cloud accounting REST API. Covers invoices, contacts, accounts, bank transactions.

coupa.notes: Coupa Business Spend Management platform. Covers procurement, invoicing, expenses, and inventory.

medius.notes: Medius AP automation platform for invoice processing and supplier management.

jack-henry-jxchange.notes: Jack Henry & Associates jXchange platform for banking core integration (accounts, transactions, teller operations).

epicor.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with Epicor REST API (OData v4). Covers all business objects — GL, AR, AP, Inventory, Production.

infor-cloudsuite.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with Infor ION API Gateway. CloudSuite Industrial, ERP, M3, LN. ION BODs for async.

acumatica.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with Acumatica REST/OData API. Covers GL, AP, AR, Inventory, Projects, CRM.

sage-intacct.notes: No dedicated connector. Use SOAP connector with Intacct XML API. Session-based auth. Covers GL, AP, AR, Inventory, Projects.

syspro.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with SYSPRO Web Services or REST API. Manufacturing-focused ERP.

sage-x3.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with Sage X3 Web Services (SOAP) or JSON REST API. Mid-market ERP.

deltek.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with Deltek REST API. Project-based ERP for government contractors and professional services.

microsoft-dynamics-365.notes: Covers Dynamics 365 CRM (Sales, Service, Marketing). Uses Microsoft Dataverse REST API.

marketo.notes: Adobe Marketo Engage marketing automation REST API.

microsoft-dynamics-crm.notes: Microsoft Dynamics CRM (on-premises or Online). For Dynamics 365 Online use the microsoft-dynamics-365 connector.

microsoft-dynamics-business-central.notes: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central ERP (SMB-focused ERP). OData REST API.

microsoft-dynamics-ax.notes: Microsoft Dynamics AX 2012 (on-premises). Legacy ERP — for newer on-premises use D365FO.

microsoft-dynamics-gp.notes: Microsoft Dynamics GP (Great Plains) on-premises ERP. Uses GP Web Services.

microsoft-dynamics-nav.notes: Microsoft Dynamics NAV (precursor to Business Central) OData endpoint.

zendesk.notes: Zendesk Support, Help Center, and Chat REST APIs. Covers tickets, users, organizations, macros.

shopify.notes: Shopify REST Admin API and GraphQL API. Covers orders, products, customers, inventory.

stripe.notes: Stripe payments platform REST API. Covers charges, customers, subscriptions, payment intents, webhooks.

braintree.notes: Braintree (PayPal subsidiary) payments platform. GraphQL and REST API. Covers transactions, vaults, subscriptions.

intercom.notes: Intercom customer messaging platform REST API. Covers contacts, conversations, companies, events.

adobe-commerce-magento.notes: Adobe Commerce (formerly Magento 2) REST API. Covers catalog, orders, customers, inventory.

hubspot-crm.notes: HubSpot CRM (Contacts, Companies, Deals, Tickets). Same connector as HubSpot Marketing. Free CRM tier available.

zoho-crm.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with Zoho CRM REST API v6. Covers leads, contacts, accounts, deals, modules.

pipedrive.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with api_token query param. Covers deals, persons, organizations, activities, pipelines.

freshsales.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with Authorization header (Token token=API_KEY). Covers contacts, accounts, deals, leads.

sugarcrm.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with SugarCRM REST API v11. Covers all modules via metadata-driven endpoints.

outreach.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with Bearer token. Covers prospects, sequences, accounts, opportunities.

authOptions: unknown — to be confirmed by Architect
spiff.notes: stub — Spiff is a Sales Performance Management / Commission platform. No MuleSoft native connector confirmed as of 2026-05-11. Integration likely requires HTTP connector via Spiff REST API. Auth type and API availability must be confirmed before architecture begins.

gravity-forms.notes: stub — No MuleSoft native connector for WordPress or Gravity Forms. Inbound integration: Gravity Forms Webhook Add-On POSTs form submissions to a MuleSoft HTTP listener (Pattern J). Requires Gravity Forms Developer or Elite license for Webhook Add-On. Outbound: use HTTP connector against WordPress REST API. Auth: inbound uses HMAC signature validation or shared secret header. Created for MRN engagement 2026-05-11.

pharmacyhub.auth: unknown — to be confirmed by Architect
pharmacyhub.notes: stub — PharmacyHub is a pharmaceutical utilization data vendor for GPO clients (aesthetics/med spa vertical). No MuleSoft native connector. Integration via SFTP file drop (Pattern E: file-based-etl). File format unknown — confirm in intake. Created for MRN engagement 2026-05-11.

pipeline-medical.auth: unknown — to be confirmed by Architect
pipeline-medical.notes: stub — Pipeline Medical is a pharmaceutical/medical utilization data vendor for GPO clients. No MuleSoft native connector. Integration via SFTP file drop (Pattern E: file-based-etl). Separate flow from PharmacyHub — no-combine rule applies. Created for MRN engagement 2026-05-11.

hd-portal.notes: stub — Home Depot Service Center (HD Portal) is HD's proprietary lead management and contract system for Pro contractor partners. No MuleSoft native connector. Use HTTP connector with API key auth. GET endpoints confirmed (Apr 2026, Peerless engagement). Write endpoints (POST/PATCH) not yet tested — required for Salesforce→HD Portal sync flow. Document download endpoint (299A/299B PDFs) not yet confirmed. API access brokered through client's HD partner contact. Created for Peerless engagement 2026-05-11. See standards/playbooks/hd-portal/hd-portal_playbook.json.

computerease.auth: unknown — to be confirmed via Deltek support
computerease.notes: stub — ComputerEase by Deltek is a Windows-based job costing and accounting system for specialty/trade contractors (fencing, roofing, HVAC, etc.). NOT the same as Deltek Costpoint or Vantagepoint (see 'deltek' entry — that is for govt contractors). No MuleSoft native connector. CRITICAL: API does NOT expose endpoints directly to internet — traffic routes through Deltek CE Live Service installed on client VM → Deltek routing servers → CE application. CE Live Service must be installed by Deltek support before any development begins. API not available in sandbox (P3) — production API only. Hosted on client GCP VM (Windows). v1.00. Created for Peerless engagement 2026-05-11. See standards/playbooks/computerease/computerease_playbook.json.

servicenow.notes: Metadata does NOT work with OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code. Use basic auth for metadata resolution. Supports custom tables and installed plugins.

jira.notes: Jira Cloud and Jira Server REST API. For Jira Cloud use API token, not password.

docuware.notes: stub — No dedicated MuleSoft connector. Use HTTP connector with token auth. REST API + Postman collections available at developer.docuware.com. Not in active integration scope for CAS; document archive only.

bmc-remedy.notes: BMC Remedy ITSM platform. Covers incidents, problems, changes via AR System REST/SOAP.

trello.notes: Trello project management boards, lists, and cards REST API.

smartsheet.notes: Smartsheet collaborative work management platform REST API. Covers sheets, rows, columns, attachments.

clickup.notes: ClickUp project management REST API. Covers tasks, lists, spaces, workflows.

freshdesk.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP Basic auth (API key as username, X as password). Covers tickets, contacts, agents, companies.

freshservice.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP Basic auth. IT service management. Covers incidents, service requests, assets, CMDB.

manageengine.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with authtoken query param (v2) or OAuth2 (v3). Covers requests, problems, changes, assets.

pagerduty-itsm.notes: No dedicated connector. PagerDuty REST API for incident management workflows. See monitoring_observability.pagerduty for Events API.

anypoint-mq.notes: MuleSoft-native managed messaging. Supports standard queues, FIFO queues, message exchanges. Has built-in circuit breaker. Supports prefetch (max throughput) and polling modes. Cross-region failover available. Requires Anypoint MQ license/subscription.

kafka.notes: Full Apache Kafka producer and consumer. Includes Confluent Schema Registry support via separate connector.

confluent-schema-registry.notes: Used alongside Kafka connector for Avro/Protobuf schema management.

amqp.notes: AMQP 0-9-1 protocol. Primarily used with RabbitMQ. Supports exchanges, queues, bindings.

jms.notes: Generic JMS 1.1 / 2.0 connector. Works with ActiveMQ, IBM MQ, Oracle AQ, and any JMS-compatible broker. Requires JMS provider JAR on classpath.

azure-service-bus.notes: Supports queues, topics, and subscriptions. Service Bus Management connector is separate (for admin ops).

azure-event-hubs.notes: Azure real-time event streaming. Good for high-throughput event ingestion scenarios.

amazon-sqs.notes: Amazon Simple Queue Service. Standard and FIFO queues. Supports visibility timeout, long polling, dead-letter queues.

amazon-sns.notes: Amazon Simple Notification Service. Fan-out messaging to multiple endpoints (SQS, Lambda, HTTP, email, SMS).

amazon-kinesis.notes: Real-time data streaming. Use for high-throughput event ingestion from IoT, logs, clickstreams.

mcp.notes: Enables Mule apps to act as MCP server OR MCP client. Supports Streamable HTTP (recommended) and SSE transport. Distributed tracing supported. Streamable HTTP supports horizontal scaling/load balancing.

ibm-mq.notes: IBM MQ (formerly MQ Series) enterprise messaging. Requires IBM MQ client JAR (com.ibm.mq.allclient.jar). Supports queues, topics, XA transactions.

mqtt.notes: MQTT 3.1.1 protocol connector for IoT messaging. Supports publish/subscribe with QoS levels 0, 1, 2.

vm.notes: In-memory (JVM) queue for intra-app messaging. Supports persistent (transient) and non-persistent queues. Use for decoupling sub-flows within the same Mule app. NOT cluster-aware — use Anypoint MQ for distributed scenarios.

google-pubsub.notes: Google Cloud Pub/Sub real-time messaging. Supports publish and subscribe to topics and subscriptions.

database.displayName: Database (Generic — MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, MSSQL, MariaDB)
database.notes: One connector handles all JDBC-compatible databases. Use specific sub-templates per DB type. Connection pooling built-in. Supports streaming for large result sets.

mongodb.notes: Supports MongoDB Atlas and self-hosted. GridFS supported for large file operations.

amazon-dynamodb.notes: AWS managed NoSQL key-value and document database.

amazon-rds.notes: Amazon RDS management connector (create/manage DB instances). For data operations use the Database connector with the RDS endpoint.

amazon-redshift.notes: AWS data warehouse. Use for analytics/reporting integrations. JDBC-based — can also use Database connector.

redis.notes: Used for caching, session management, pub/sub, rate limiting. Can be used as custom Object Store backend.

cassandra.notes: Apache Cassandra and DataStax distributed NoSQL database.

azure-cosmos-db.notes: Multi-model NoSQL database. Supports SQL, MongoDB, Cassandra, Gremlin, Table APIs.

neo4j.notes: Neo4j graph database via Bolt protocol. Use for knowledge graphs, recommendation engines, fraud detection.

snowflake.notes: Snowflake cloud data warehouse. JDBC-based. Can also use Database connector with Snowflake JDBC driver.

hadoop-hdfs.notes: Apache Hadoop HDFS connector. Use for data lake integrations with on-premises Hadoop clusters.

reltio.notes: Reltio cloud-native Master Data Management (MDM) platform. Use for golden record management and entity resolution.

database-mysql.notes: MySQL-specific variant of the generic Database connector. Includes mysql-connector-j driver.

database-postgresql.notes: PostgreSQL-specific variant of the generic Database connector. Includes postgresql JDBC driver.

database-sqlserver.notes: SQL Server variant of the generic Database connector. Includes mssql-jdbc driver.

database-oracle.notes: Oracle DB variant of the generic Database connector. Includes ojdbc11 driver. Use service name not SID for modern configs. IMPORTANT: ojdbc11.jar cannot be in pom.xml due to Oracle license — must be placed in shared lib folder on CloudHub 2.0.

database-db2.notes: IBM DB2 variant of the generic Database connector. Includes IBM JCC driver. Common in mainframe integration scenarios.

database-saphana.notes: SAP HANA variant of the generic Database connector. Includes ngdbc driver. Used for real-time analytics and SAP S/4HANA embedded analytics.

database-mariadb.notes: MariaDB variant of the generic Database connector. Includes MariaDB Connector/J driver. MySQL-compatible.

influxdb.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with Bearer token. Time-series database for metrics and IoT data. Line Protocol for writes; Flux for queries.

databricks.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with Bearer token or Database connector with Simba JDBC driver for SQL queries on Delta tables.

file.notes: Local file system access. Used for batch file processing, archiving, temp storage. WARNING: CloudHub 2.0 local filesystem is ephemeral — use S3, SFTP, or Azure Blob for any persistence requirement.

ftp.notes: Plain FTP. Prefer SFTP for any sensitive data.

sftp.notes: Secure FTP over SSH. Preferred for all file transfers involving sensitive data.

amazon-s3.notes: AWS object storage. Used for large file/binary transfers, data lake integration, batch file exchange.

azure-blob.notes: Azure Blob, Queue, and Table storage.

azure-data-lake.notes: Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 for big data analytics.

box.notes: Box cloud content management and file sharing.

dropbox.notes: Dropbox Business and personal cloud storage.

smb.notes: Server Message Block (SMB) protocol for Windows file shares (CIFS/SMB2/SMB3). Alternative to SFTP for Windows-native file exchange.

microsoft-sharepoint.notes: Microsoft SharePoint Online and on-premises. Covers lists, libraries, files, workflows. Use Microsoft Graph API (HTTP connector) for modern SPO.

microsoft-onedrive.notes: Microsoft OneDrive and OneDrive for Business via Microsoft Graph API.

laserfiche.notes: Laserfiche Enterprise Content Management (ECM) platform. Covers document capture, storage, retrieval, workflows.

email.notes: Supports SMTP, SMTPS, IMAP, IMAPS, POP3. Use for outbound notifications from error handlers and scheduled reports.

gmail.notes: Gmail-specific connector using Google OAuth 2.0. For generic SMTP use the Email connector.

twilio.notes: Twilio cloud communications platform. Covers SMS, voice calls, WhatsApp, email (SendGrid), Verify API.

slack.notes: Slack messaging platform API. Covers messages, channels, users, files, slash commands, workflows.

microsoft-teams.notes: Microsoft Teams messaging via Microsoft Graph API. Covers channels, messages, meetings, files.

microsoft-outlook-365.notes: Microsoft Outlook 365 email and calendar via Microsoft Graph API. Covers mail, calendar events, contacts.

zoom.notes: Zoom video conferencing REST API. Covers meetings, webinars, users, recordings. Use Server-to-Server OAuth (replaces JWT in 2023).

mailchimp.notes: Mailchimp email marketing platform REST API. Covers lists, campaigns, members, automations.

amazon-lambda.notes: Invoke AWS Lambda functions from Mule flows.

amazon-ec2.notes: Amazon EC2 management — start/stop instances, manage security groups etc.

amazon-bedrock.notes: AWS generative AI models (Claude, Titan, Llama, etc.) via Amazon Bedrock API.

amazon-secrets-manager.notes: Retrieves secrets from AWS Secrets Manager for use as Mule properties. Alternative to Anypoint Secrets Manager for AWS-native environments.

amazon-ses.notes: Amazon Simple Email Service. Transactional and bulk email. Alt to Email connector for AWS-native envs.

amazon-cloudwatch.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with AWS SigV4 signing to push custom metrics and query alarms.

amazon-cognito.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP for user management and token validation.

amazon-api-gateway.notes: Gateway layer — not a target system. Use HTTP connector to call APIs deployed behind API Gateway.

amazon-ecs.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP to trigger task runs and query service status via ECS API.

amazon-step-functions.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with SigV4 to start/query executions. Good for async orchestration from Mule.

azure-key-vault.notes: Retrieve secrets, keys, and certificates from Azure Key Vault. Also available as properties provider.

azure-key-vault-properties.notes: Use Azure Key Vault secrets as Mule application properties directly.

azure-service-bus-management.notes: Azure Service Bus management plane operations (create/delete queues, topics, subscriptions). Different from the messaging connector which handles data plane send/receive.

microsoft-excel-online.notes: Microsoft Excel Online via Microsoft Graph API. Read/write workbooks, worksheets, tables, ranges stored in OneDrive or SharePoint.

azure-active-directory.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with Microsoft Graph API for users, groups, directory operations.

azure-cognitive-services.notes: Azure AI Services (Vision, Language, Speech, OpenAI). Use HTTP with Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key per service.

azure-functions.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP trigger endpoint with function key. Analogous to Amazon Lambda.

azure-api-management.notes: Gateway layer — not a target system. Use HTTP with subscription key to call APIs exposed via APIM.

azure-monitor.notes: Azure Monitor (Log Analytics, App Insights, Metrics). Use HTTP to query logs or ingest custom metrics.

edifact.notes: EDIFACT EDI parsing and generation. UN/EDIFACT standard.

as2.notes: AS2 (Applicability Statement 2) B2B messaging protocol. Primary transport for secure EDI exchange. APM-aware — when used inside an Anypoint Partner Manager flow, partner AS2 IDs and certificates are resolved dynamically from APM instead of static config. Supports MDN (Message Disposition Notification) acknowledgement, synchronous and asynchronous MDN.

a2a.notes: Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol connector for Agentforce multi-agent orchestration. Implements the open A2A standard (co-authored by Google/Salesforce) for autonomous AI agents to communicate and delegate tasks. Use alongside the Agentforce connector for building agentic workflows. Category placed in edi_b2b historically but now primarily used for AI agent networking.

rosettanet.notes: RosettaNet Partner Interface Processes (PIPs) for supply chain B2B.

x12.notes: ANSI X12 EDI parsing and generation. Covers 850 PO, 810 Invoice, 856 ASN, 855 PO Ack, 997 FA and hundreds more transaction sets. Requires schema definitions.

tradacoms.notes: TRADACOMS EDI standard (UK retail industry). Used primarily in UK supply chain integrations.

hl7.notes: HL7 v2.x message parsing and generation. Used for healthcare system integration (ADT, ORM, ORU, etc.). For HL7 MLLP transport use the hl7-mllp connector.

hl7-mllp.notes: HL7 Minimal Lower Layer Protocol (MLLP) transport. Required for connecting to EHR/HIS systems (Epic, Cerner, etc.) that communicate over raw TCP sockets.

mulesoft-vectors.notes: Connects to vector databases and embedding models for RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) use cases. Supports Pinecone, Weaviate, OpenAI embeddings etc.

mulesoft-ai-chain.notes: MuleSoft AI Chain connector — orchestrates LLM calls with tool use, chains, and memory. Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI as providers.

inference.notes: MuleSoft Inference connector for calling hosted ML model endpoints. Supports REST-based inference APIs.

chatgpt.notes: OpenAI ChatGPT API connector. Covers chat completions, embeddings. Consider using MuleSoft AI Chain connector for more advanced LLM orchestration.

mulesoft-forge-idp.notes: PREFERRED for IDP. MuleSoft Forge universal IDP connector — works across all action versions without connector sprawl. Operations: Service IDP - Execution - Submit, Service IDP - Execution Result - Retrieve. Auth: Anypoint Connected App OAuth 2.0 client credentials. Scope: leave empty (permissions controlled by Connected App scopes). Requires Mule 4.6+. Available on Maven Central (NOT Anypoint Exchange) — add mavenCentral() repo to pom.xml. Released Sept 2025.

anypoint-idp.displayName: Anypoint IDP via HTTP (Fallback — use mulesoft-forge-idp instead)
anypoint-idp.notes: FALLBACK — prefer mulesoft-forge-idp connector. Raw HTTP calls to IDP REST API. Base URL: https://idp-rt.{region}.anypoint.mulesoft.com/api/v1/ (regions: us-east-1, eu-central-1). POST submit: body={file:<base64>, fileName:<name.pdf>}. GET poll: /executions/{id}/v2 (note /v2 suffix). Status values: ACKNOWLEDGED|IN_PROGRESS|RESULTS_PENDING|SUCCEEDED|FAILED|PARTIAL_SUCCESS|MANUAL_VALIDATION_REQUIRED. Results in pages[].fields[]. OAuth scope: leave empty (Connected App permissions control access). Min polling interval: 10s per IDP quota docs. Token URL: https://anypoint.mulesoft.com/accounts/api/v2/oauth2/token. Max file: 10MB, 50 pages. P50 latency: 7.6s, P99: 13.4s.

caqh.notes: CAQH provider credentialing and data sharing. Healthcare-specific compliance connector.

kno2.notes: Kno2 healthcare interoperability network for clinical document exchange (C-CDA, Direct messaging, FHIR).

redox.notes: Redox healthcare data platform for EHR connectivity. Normalizes clinical data across HL7, FHIR, and proprietary formats.

verato-umpi.notes: Verato Universal Master Patient Index for patient identity resolution and matching across healthcare systems.

epic-ehr.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with Epic FHIR R4 API. SMART on FHIR OAuth2 for backend service apps. Covers patients, encounters, observations, conditions.

cerner-oracle-health.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with Cerner FHIR R4 API. SMART on FHIR backend services auth. Covers patients, encounters, medications, labs.

athenahealth.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with OAuth2. Covers patients, appointments, clinical, billing via athenaNet REST API.

allscripts.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with Allscripts Unity API or FHIR R4 endpoint.

http.notes: Use for any REST API not in registry. HTTP Listener for inbound, HTTP Requester for outbound. Always configure responseTimeout explicitly. Default 10 seconds.

soap.notes: Use for any SOAP/WSDL service not in registry. Store WSDL in resources/api/{system}.wsdl. Supports WS-Security.

websocket.notes: Bidirectional full-duplex communication. Use for real-time push notifications, live dashboards.

ldap.notes: LDAP directory access. Used for Active Directory integration, user provisioning, authentication lookups.

object-store.notes: Key-value persistent/in-memory storage. Use for watermarking, token caching, session state, idempotency. Supports TTL. CloudHub uses managed Object Store v2.

cloudhub.notes: Manage CloudHub 1.0 applications and alerts from within a Mule flow. Use for ops automation (restart apps, update properties, send notifications). CloudHub 2.0 deployments are managed via Anypoint Runtime Manager REST API (use HTTP connector) — there is no separate CH2 connector. Requires Anypoint Platform credentials.

sockets.notes: Raw TCP and UDP socket connections. Use for custom protocols, legacy system integration, HL7 MLLP (prefer dedicated MLLP connector), and custom binary protocols.

ibm-ctg.notes: IBM CICS Transaction Gateway for mainframe CICS program integration. Requires IBM CTG client libraries. Supports COMMAREA and channel/container calls.

microsoft-dotnet.notes: Invoke .NET assemblies directly from Mule flows. Uses a .NET bridge process. Only works on Windows or with a Windows remote host.

microsoft-powershell.notes: Execute PowerShell scripts on remote Windows hosts via WinRM. Use for Windows server automation, Active Directory management.

grpc.notes: gRPC protocol connector. Supports unary and streaming calls. Requires .proto service definition.

anypoint-custom-metrics.notes: Sends custom business metrics (gauges, counters) to Anypoint Monitoring dashboards. Requires Titanium subscription. Use in flows to track domain KPIs (order count, error rate by partner, SLA breaches) alongside built-in Mule runtime metrics. Works alongside Anypoint Visualizer (which auto-discovers topology — no connector needed for Visualizer).

aggregators.notes: Time-based and size-based message aggregation. Use for batching upstream events before downstream processing.

cryptography.notes: Encrypt/decrypt payloads (PGP, JCE, XML) and sign/verify messages. Required for regulated patterns.

compression.notes: Compress and decompress payloads (ZIP, GZIP, TAR). Use in file-based ETL and large-payload flows.

java.notes: Invoke Java methods and constructors from DataWeave or XML. Use for helper libraries that cannot be expressed in DataWeave.

json.notes: JSON schema validation. Use json:validate-schema to reject invalid payloads at API boundary before processing.

kerberos.notes: Kerberos ticket acquisition. Required for Hadoop HDFS, enterprise AD-integrated systems, and some on-prem database/LDAP auth.

oauth.notes: Mule OAuth 2.0 provider and token validation. Use when building APIs that accept OAuth tokens from external identity providers.

google-analytics.notes: Google Analytics 4 Reporting API. Fetch dimensions, metrics, reports for business intelligence integrations.

tableau.notes: Tableau REST API and Hyper API. Publish data sources, refresh extracts, manage workbooks and views.

power-bi.notes: Microsoft Power BI REST API. Push data to streaming datasets, manage reports, refresh datasets.

splunk.notes: Splunk data platform REST API. Send events, search indexes, manage inputs. Use for operational intelligence and SIEM integration.

looker.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with OAuth2. Covers Looks, dashboard tiles, data exploration via Looker API 4.0.

dbt-cloud.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with Authorization header. Trigger dbt Cloud jobs, retrieve run status and artifacts.

automation-anywhere.notes: Trigger and monitor Automation Anywhere RPA bots from Mule flows. NOTE: This is the Automation Anywhere (AA360) connector — a third-party RPA platform. MuleSoft RPA (native product based on Servicetrace) does NOT have a dedicated Mule connector — MuleSoft RPA bots are triggered via the MuleSoft RPA REST API using the HTTP connector.

blue-prism.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with Blue Prism Hub API or Control Room API to start/monitor robot processes.

kofax-rpa.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP with Kofax RPA Management Console REST API to schedule and run robots.

microsoft-power-automate.notes: No dedicated connector. Use HTTP to trigger Power Automate flows via HTTP Request trigger endpoint. Useful for hybrid Mule + Power Platform scenarios.

dw-jwt-library.notes: DataWeave functions for generating and validating JSON Web Tokens (JWT). Import via: import jwt from data-weave-jwt-library. Covers HS256, RS256 signing. Useful for outbound API auth token generation without needing a Java helper.

dw-analytics-library.notes: Collection of DataWeave functions for data analysis: statistical aggregations, percentiles, histograms, moving averages, correlation. Use in Transform Message for inline analytics without external tools.

dw-slack-library.notes: DataWeave helpers for building Slack Block Kit message payloads. Use with the Slack connector or HTTP requester to compose rich Slack notification messages without manual JSON construction.

dw-mock-data-generators.notes: DataWeave functions for generating realistic mock/fake data: names, emails, addresses, phone numbers, UUIDs, dates. Use in MUnit tests or scaffolded dev environments to generate test payloads without hardcoding.

apm-payload-storage-s3.notes: REQUIRED for APM: Every APM deployment needs a Payload Storage API — a Mule app you build and deploy that APM calls to store/retrieve B2B message payloads. This is the recommended S3-backed implementation template. Deploy it to CloudHub and register the URL in APM settings. Alternative implementations: MySQL (apm-payload-storage-service-mysql-template) and Object Store (apm-payload-storage-service-obj-store).

apm-payload-storage-db.notes: Alternative APM Payload Storage implementation using a relational database (MySQL or PostgreSQL). Use when S3 is unavailable or a relational store is preferred for payload retention and querying. Implements the same Partner Manager Content Storage API contract.

apm-payload-storage-object-store.displayName: APM Payload Storage — Object Store Implementation
apm-payload-storage-object-store.notes: Lightweight APM Payload Storage implementation using Anypoint Object Store v2. Suitable for dev/test environments or low-volume scenarios. Not recommended for production — Object Store has size and retention limits. For production use S3 or Database implementations.

anypoint-rpa.notes: No dedicated Mule connector JAR. Uses HTTP connector against Anypoint RPA REST API v2 (OAuth) or v1 (API key). Production MUST use OAuth 2.0 client credentials with Connected App scopes: 'RPA Integrator' + 'RPA Invocable Process'. API key is user-scoped, expires, and must NOT be used in production. Idempotent invocation via PUT /executions/startProcess (same executionId = no duplicate run). Poll status via GET every 30s. See standards/scenarios/rpa-orchestration.md for full pattern.
